geography: Maastricht type area, the Netherlands (latest Maastrichtian Mosasaurus sample)

regionalRanges.label: Dallasaurus middle Turonian occurrence
regionalRanges.basis: The stage envelope captures the middle Turonian Dallasaurus skeletons without treating them as a globally complete family range.

overview: Bell and Polcyn's sampled Mosasauridae includes both plesiopedal Dallasaurus and more derived hydropedal members; limb grade alone is not treated as a family diagnosis.

ecology.diet: Marine carnivore; diet varied among sampled taxa
ecology.habitat: Marine; sampled foraging habitat varied by taxon
ecology.locomotion: Plesiopedal to hydropedal limb adaptations across sampled lineages
ecology.bodySize: Small plesiopedal to much larger hydropedal forms
ecology.guild: Marine carnivores with resource partitioning in the sampled Maastrichtian fauna

traits: Mosasauridae includes plesiopedal as well as hydropedal members in the cited analysis
Dallasaurus preserves cranial, axial and limb characters in two incomplete skeletons
Plesiopedal and hydropedal limb conditions occur in separate sampled lineages
evidenceSummary: The Dallasaurus skeletons, a 144-character phylogenetic analysis, a five-taxon isotope sample and a latest-Maastrichtian skull separately constrain morphology, limb-grade evolution, sampled ecology and the displayed occurrence envelope.
